A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–G are available and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original penetration-testing evaluations, including task completion, failure analysis, human intervention and augmentation results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical evaluations and results, including the detailed tables and examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: The agent architectures and five augmentations—GCM, IAM, CCI, AP and RTM—retain the same procedures. Rewording in Section 6 and Appendix F.2 does not change their operation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven penetration-testing task categories and the same 14 machines from HackTheBox, Metasploitable and VulnHub listed in Table 8. Appendix scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4/ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, AutoAttacker, PentestGPT and PenHeal, including the same augmented configurations. Newly cited research is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix F retain the same metrics, sequential task procedure, success/failure criteria and model configurations. Temperature 0.8, top-p 1.0, the 2048-token limit and machine-level subtask counts are unchanged.

E4.justification: The augmentation comparisons, failure-cause breakdowns, context-retention analysis, oversight analyses and appendix case studies are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–6 and the plotted findings match. For example, Table 3 retains baseline SCR values of 25.9%, 41.2% and 52.1% for the three modular agents, and Table 5 retains zero MITM success for every evaluated agent.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and their definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces mathematical proofs or theorems; the added antifragility discussion is conceptual motivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about functional capabilities, recurring failures and benefits of the five augmentations. Added literature connections do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 newly interprets the observed failures as consistent with broader findings about multi-agent misalignment and coordination breakdowns, citing Cemri et al. (2025). Existing mechanism explanations, applicability boundaries and the Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the same API access descriptions, hyperparameters, agent configurations and evaluation instructions. Appendix command examples are reformatted without substantive technical changes; no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and connections to antifragile AI safety, hallucination research, ReAct and multi-agent failure research. It also separately cites the preprint of the already cited Lost in the Middle work. These are limited additions to the existing positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes sentence-level and punctuation edits, adds brief introductory and concluding passages and an acknowledgement, and updates author order, affiliations and correspondence information. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are reflowed, including Table 1 moving from PDF page 5 to 6 and Figure 7 from page 14 to 15. Appendix listings use more compact typography without line numbers, and page numbers disappear. Figures and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds modest literature context and funding transparency while retaining the same scientific evidence, reproducibility information and limitations. Presentation changes are mixed: appendix listings become more compact, but some prose edits introduce grammatical problems, notably the fragmented MITM discussion in Section 7. These small editorial gains and defects leave overall quality essentially unchanged.
